title: SQL Developer
description:
Pay Rate: $74.00 - $78.00 Negotiable based upon years of experience

Global Financial Firm located in IRVING, TX has an immediate contract opportunity for an experienced SQL Developer

Responsibilities:

  • Write and optimize advanced queries, views, and scripts to support application development and data analysis.
  • Develop and manage data access layers and backend database logic.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • 5-10 years of professional experience as a SQL Developer or in a similar database-focused role.
  • Expert proficiency in SQL and Oracle databases, including extensive experience with PL/SQL, stored procedures, functions, and performance tuning.
  • Hands-on experience with MongoDB, including a strong understanding of MQL, indexing, and the aggregation framework.
  • Proven experience in data modeling for both relational (Oracle) and NoSQL (MongoDB) databases.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot complex database issues.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with cloud-based database services such as Oracle Cloud, AWS RDS, or MongoDB Atlas.
  • Knowledge of ETL tools (e.g., Informatica, Talend, SSIS).
  • Proficiency in scripting languages like Python, Bash, or PowerShell for automation.
  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies.
  • Experience with version control systems, such as Git.
  • Knowledge of other database technologies is a plus.

Key Responsibilities:

Infection Prevention Liaisons (IPLs) monitor hand hygiene practices, staff compliance with isolation precautions and personal protective equipment and conduct quality assurance checks for share mobile equipment in various areas in the hospital across all eight NYP campuses. IPLs are trained and validated to conduct direct observations, which is the gold standard in monitoring hand hygiene and other infection prevention practices. In addition to conducting hand hygiene observations, they also educate healthcare workers about any missed hand hygiene or other infection prevention opportunities. After educating HCWs about missed opportunities, IPLs document and communicate the results of their observations to supervisors, managers and Patient Care Directors (PCDs), medical directors and other hospital leaders. IPLs report directly to the Program Manager for Infection Prevention & Control Department.

Infection Prevention & Control Liaisons conduct direct observations, which is the gold standard in monitoring hand hygiene and other infection prevention practices to satisfy Joint Commission, CMS and the Department of Health standards.

In exercising these functions, the person must be able to lift 50 lbs., manipulate 400 lb. drums, and be physically able to wear respiratory protection. Environments range from usual office conditions to environments where "immediately dangerous to life and health" (IDLH) atmospheres exist requiring the use of burdensome protective clothing and equipment. Where not extremely hazardous, work may be uncomfortable or unpleasant (i.e. high heat).
